papers.title: Colossal Terahertz Magnetoresistance from Magnetic Polarons in EuZn 2 P 2
papers.authors: E. Marulanda, M. Dutra, N. M. Kawahala, E. D. Stefanato, G. G. Vasques, J. Munevar, M. A. Avila, F. G. G. Hernandez
papers.abstract: Magnetic polarons can generate colossal magnetoresistance in magnetic semiconductors, yet their terahertz electrodynamics remain largely unexplored. Here we report magneto-terahertz spectroscopy of the Eu-based Zintl antiferromagnet EuZn 2 P 2 . The low-frequency conductivity shows pronounced non-Drude behavior consistent with an evolution from isolated to overlapping magnetic polarons upon cooling. The polaron relaxation time reaches a maximum near the Néel temperature at zero field and exhibits a strong magnetic-field dependence. This polaron-driven reshaping of the conductivity leads to a strongly frequency-dependent magnetoresistance that becomes colossal in the terahertz range, reaching about 90 % at 1.5 THz, roughly three times larger than the zero-frequency limit value. These results demonstrate that magnetic polarons strongly govern the low-energy electrodynamics and highlight the sensitivity of terahertz spectroscopy to polaronic magnetotransport in correlated magnetic semiconductors.

papers.title: Microscopic Theory of Spin Polarons in Chern Ferromagnets
papers.authors: Qiang Gao, Eslam Khalaf
papers.abstract: We develop a microscopic theory of charged excitations in an SU(2) Chern ferromagnet and obtain closed-form wavefunctions for a hierarchy of charge-$e$ spin polaron states binding an arbitrary number of spin flips. In an ideal Chern-$1$ band with a normal-ordered contact interaction, we show that these polarons are exact eigenstates of the Hamiltonian with the same energy as single-hole excitations. Away from this ideal limit, we promote these states to a variational family by introducing a single size parameter and a geometry-informed single-particle dressing. Our momentum-space wavefunctions admit two equivalent representations: a ratio of Jastrow factors of Weierstrass functions of relative momenta or an antisymmetrized geminal product of particle-hole wavefunctions. The latter enables efficient evaluation of overlaps and expectation values for large system sizes and many spin flips. Benchmarking in the lowest Landau level, the single-spin-flip ansatz achieves $\gtrsim 99\%$ overlap with exact diagonalization and accurately captures binding energies, while the multi-spin-flip energies interpolate smoothly toward the large-texture (skyrmion) regime. For Chern bands with tunable quantum geometry, we find that interaction-generated single particle dispersion quickly destabilizes the spin polarons once quantum geometry becomes sufficiently non-uniform. When such dispersion is suppressed, however, the bound states persist deeper into the non-uniform regime, with the binding energy slowly decreasing and the bound state becoming larger as the quantum geometry becomes more concentrated. Our results provide a microscopic foundation for analyzing doped Chern ferromagnets in moiré platforms and lay the groundwork for variational wavefunctions of multi-polaron excitations and phases.

papers.title: Spin Excitons Modulated by Magnetic Orders in a Magnetic Weyl Semimetal NdAlSi
papers.authors: Bo Zhang, Junbo Liao, Lihao Xia, Zhentao Huang, Yanyan Shangguan, Shufan Cheng, Hao Xu, Zihang Song, Shuai Dong, Maofeng Wu, Wei Wang, Ryoichi Kajimoto, Mitsutaka Nakamura, Song Bao, Zhao-Yang Dong, Shun-Li Yu, Jian-Xin Li, Jinsheng Wen
papers.abstract: We report the observation of dispersive spin excitons in the rare-earth magnetic Weyl semimetal NdAlSi through comprehensive thermodynamic and inelastic neutron scattering measurements. Notably, the behavior of spin excitons is strongly modulated by magnetic order: they remain dispersive in the paramagnetic phase, shift to higher energies and broaden in the incommensurate antiferromagnetic phase, and split into distinct branches in the commensurate ferrimagnetic phase. To elucidate the microscopic origin of this evolution, we construct an effective crystal electric field (CEF)–exchange model and calculate the excitation spectra within the random-phase approximation. This framework consistently accounts for the observed excitation dispersions and mode splitting by incorporating two magnetic-order-dependent effects: an effective renormalization of the local CEF environment associated with the concomitant reconstruction of the itinerant electronic structure across the magnetic phases, and exchange-generated molecular fields that lift the Kramers degeneracy. Our findings reveal the interplay among localized 4f states, itinerant electrons, and magnetic order, and establish NdAlSi as a model platform for studying collective CEF excitations in rare-earth quantum materials.

papers.title: Supersolid crystals of dipolar excitons in a lattice
papers.authors: C. Morin, C. Lagoin, T. Gupta, N. Reinić, A. Gupta, K. Baldwin, L. Pfeiffer, G. Pupillo, F. Dubin
papers.abstract: In condensed-matter physics, long-range correlations introduce quantum states of matter that challenge intuition. For example, supersolids combine density order that manifests as symmetry-breaking spatial arrangement, and frictionless superfluid flow. However, supersolids have proven to exist only under very stringent conditions, with evidence limited to a few spontaneously fragmented superfluids observed in the weakly interacting regime. Here we demonstrate a framework to realize crystalline supersolids in the strong-interaction regime, by confining dipolar bosons in a lattice with long-range hopping. We show that dipolar excitons realize this lattice model. At fractional lattice fillings of one-quarter, one-third and one-half, we observe mesoscopic quantum crystals across around 100 sites that spontaneously break the lattice translational symmetry. At the same time, coherent long-range hopping induces off-diagonal long-range order such that the exciton solids are superfluids. Our numerical methods quantitatively confirm that supersolidity builds up in the ground state of the lattice Hamiltonian. Supersolids have previously been observed in weakly interacting scenarios. Now several supersolid phases are demonstrated in a strongly correlated system of dipolar excitons confined to a lattice with long-range hopping.

papers.abstract: Modern and future electronics harbour a key challenge: as conventional metal wires shrink to nanoscale dimensions, their resistivity increases sharply1 owing to surface and grain-boundary scattering. To circumvent this unwanted behaviour, here, we explore the fundamental limits of charge transport in topological semimetal niobium phosphide (NbP) nanoribbons down to approximately 6-nm widths, with industry-friendly top-down nanofabrication. The extracted NbP nanoribbon resistivity reaches 18 ± 4.1 μΩ cm at room temperature with an approximately 9-nm2 cross-sectional area, lower than that of conventional metals and semimetals with comparable size. The NbP nanoribbon resistivity decreases with decreasing width, unlike the classical behaviour of metals such as copper. This trend suggests a growing relative contribution of surface and edge states as the nanoribbon cross-section is reduced, despite a certain amount of disorder, including edge roughness. Our findings advance the understanding of size-dependent transport and scaling in this class of semimetals, offering a platform for nanoscale wires and interconnects in future nanoelectronics. papers.abstract: Brightened symmetry-forbidden excitons can provide critical information about the electronic structure and many-body interactions in semiconductors. Recently, interlayer atomic registry has emerged as a new way to control atomically thin layered materials in both ground and excited states. Here we show that the rhombohedral stacking in a 3R-MoS_2 homobilayer can brighten two symmetry-forbidden interlayer excitons: one is a spin-unlike 1s exciton and the other is a parity-odd 2p exciton. The nature of these interlayer excitons is revealed by their gfactors as well as the hybridization patterns observed when they are tuned to resonate with intralayer excitons. Surprisingly, the hybridized 2p exciton exhibits a constructive quantum interference between the acquired transition dipoles, revealing a hidden gauge-invariant phase contrast between the constituent electronic states. Our results establish stacking control as a powerful approach for modulating quantum phases of excitons in 2D semiconductors.

papers.abstract: We investigate the topological properties of a strongly correlated moiré transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) bilayer (such as twisted $\mathrm{MoTe}_2$ or $\mathrm{WSe}_2$) hosting a spin-charge separated state coupled to a layer-polarized helical spin texture. Analyzing an effective low-energy Hamiltonian for mobile spinless holons moving through this non-coplanar spinon background, we reveal pronounced asymmetric band warping. This warping closes the global indirect band gap across most of the parameter space, restricting true topological insulators to fine-tuned critical trajectories. However, a finite local direct gap persists, stabilizing broad regions of a topological Chern metal ($C = \pm 1$). Computing the Chern number and density of states, we demonstrate that this phase naturally yields a sizable, non-quantized anomalous Hall response accompanied by finite longitudinal conduction, providing a purely electronic strong-coupling mechanism for dissipative anomalous Hall states in moiré systems.

papers.abstract: Compensated magnets provide a versatile platform for spin-dependent electronic and transport phenomena. Here, we show that magnetic reconfiguration, i.e., selective reversal of local moments without changing the underlying crystal structure, can profoundly transform the nonrelativistic spin splitting and spin-orbit-coupled responses of spin-degenerate antiferromagnets (AFMs), altermagnets (AMs), and compensated ferrimagnets (cFIMs). Strikingly, magnetic configurations with nearly degenerate energies can exhibit qualitatively different spin-split band structures and anomalous Hall responses, allowing a small magnetic-energy scale to produce large changes in physical properties. Combining tight-binding models, oriented spin space group analysis, and first-principles calculations, we demonstrate that converting an AM configuration into cFIM states activates staggered onsite-potential contributions to spin splitting, complementing the anisotropic-hopping mechanism of AMs and removing symmetry-enforced degeneracies. Moreover, cFIM symmetry permits an anomalous Hall response at first order in spin-orbit coupling, in contrast to the higher-order or orientation-constrained responses of corresponding AM states. We demonstrate this regime in Mn2Mo3O8, one of 12 cFIM candidates identified in the MAGNDATA database, and further demonstrate its generality by designing cFIMs from collinear AFMs, exemplified by MnGeO3 and Co2Mo3O8. Our results establish magnetic reconfiguration as a powerful symmetry-guided strategy for dramatically reshaping electronic and transport responses in compensated magnets.

papers.abstract: Frustrated spin chains host exotic phases beyond the Landau paradigm, yet weak first-order transitions and unconventional criticalities remain elusive. Combining large-scale density-matrix renormalization group with bosonization methods, we map the phase diagram of a spin-1 chain with next-nearest-neighbor (NNN) coupling and single-ion anisotropy (SIA). We pinpoint two topological phase transitions: a weakly first-order transition between the Haldane and NNN-Haldane phases with a tiny gap and a continuous transition from the Haldane phase to the large-$D$ phase located via level spectroscopy with Richardson extrapolation. For negative SIA, a spontaneous dimerized phase emerges between the Néel and NNN-Néel phases. Its transition into the Néel phase is a deconfined quantum critical point falling into the eight-vertex universality class, with central charge $c = 1$ and critical exponents varying continuously along the phase boundary. For positive SIA, we identify two vector-spin-chirality orders---an ordinary chiral phase and a narrow Haldane-chiral phase---with a weakly first-order transition between them, evidenced by a soft jump in the string order parameter. Our results reveal that frustration and anisotropy generate emergent orders and non-Landau criticalities, providing a platform for deconfined and topological phase transitions.

papers.abstract: Magneto-optical (MO) responses provide a direct probe of magnetic order, yet resolving compensated antiferromagnetic order remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate in altermagnetic MnTe that the symmetry of the Néel order is imprinted on the MO response through distinct quantum-geometric contributions. Combining first-principles calculations with a Landau symmetry framework, we demonstrate that the quantum metric gives rise to a twofold optical anisotropy, with its diagonal and symmetric off-diagonal components forming an $E_{2g}$ doublet associated with the quadratic Néel-order invariants, providing a characteristic MO Voigt signature of the Néel-vector orientation. In contrast, the Berry curvature generates a complementary threefold Hall response governed by the cubic $A_{2g}$ Néel-order invariant. Although the Hall conductivity and the out-of-plane weak-ferromagnetic moment share the same symmetry and angular dependence, constraining the latter to zero leaves the optical Hall response essentially unchanged demonstrating that the Hall response originates directly from the compensated Néel order rather than the net magnetization. Our results establish quantum geometry as a direct link between Néel order and MO response, revealing distinct twofold and threefold optical signatures of Néel order in altermagnetic MnTe.

papers.abstract: Motivated by recent experiments, we theoretically investigate AB-stacked WSe$_2$/MoTe$_2$ bilayers. Our theory incorporates valence fluctuations, local and extended (longer-range) Hubbard interactions, including non-local interactions between carriers on the MoTe$_2$ layer. Within the parton mean-field framework, we show that the non-local interaction between MoTe$_2$ carriers can drive a transition between a topological Kondo semimetal(TKSM) and a topological Kondo insulator(TKI) at the filling fraction $ν=2$. We attribute this transition to an emergent spin-loop current arising from the interplay between Ising spin-orbit coupling and non-local electron correlations. In addition, we investigate how the emergent spin-loop current affects edge transport and show that the two-point conductance takes a quantized value at certain bias voltages.

papers.abstract: We perform a dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) + Bethe-Salpeter equation (BSE) study of collective spin excitations in $\mathrm{La_3Ni_2O_7}$, using a bilayer two-orbital Kanamori-Hubbard model derived from density functional theory. On this basis, we apply the BSE to compute the lattice transverse spin susceptibility, which exhibits a damped spin-wave spectrum with a bandwidth of $\sim$0.1 eV and a wave vector of ($π$/2, $π$/2), in good agreement with resonant inelastic x-ray scattering and inelastic neutron scattering data. Further analysis of the irreducible vertex reveals notable frequency dependence in the $d_{z^2}$ orbital. Finally, we investigate the evolution of the spectrum with varying Hund's coupling and electron fillings. Our study bridges the localized and itinerant descriptions of spin excitations in $\mathrm{La_3Ni_2O_7}$.

papers.abstract: Strong spin-orbit coupling in $5d$ ions produces multipolar orders that conventional probes barely detect. In cubic $5d^1$ double perovskites, the spin-orbit quartet couples to Jahn-Teller vibrations, and resonant inelastic x-ray scattering (RIXS) has established the resulting spin-orbit-lattice entangled (vibronic) states [Phys. Rev. Lett. \textbf{133}, 036501 (2024)]. We proposed that these vibronic states order cooperatively and thereby explain the hidden quadrupole and canted magnetic phases of Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$ [Phys. Rev. B \textbf{107}, L220404 (2023)], but that proposal rested on a simplified model. Here, we show that a spin-vibronic Hamiltonian derived from first principles, with a single scale factor for the elastic coupling, reproduces the ordered phases of Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$ with the same vibronic states that describe its RIXS spectra. With this factor bringing the quadrupolar transition to 34.7 K, near the measured 33 K, the theory predicts the magnetic transition at 19.3 K, against the measured 18 K, and reproduces the antiferro distortion and the ferro elongation between the transitions. These results support spin-vibronic order in Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$ and point to it as the origin of the hidden multipolar phases of $5d^1$ double perovskites.

papers.abstract: Delocalized bonding electrons have long been associated with soft bonds and low phonon frequencies. However, a quantitative connection between electron delocalization and phonon softening remains elusive. We identify such a connection through the momentum-space quantum metric, which measures the intrinsic delocalization of the occupied electronic states. We show that a quantum geometric contribution to phonon softening is proportional to the integrated quantum metric. First-principles calculations of more than a hundred compounds demonstrate that greater quantum metric generally accompanies softer phonons. Localized Wannier orbitals reveal the bonding environments associated with this delocalization. In ferroelectric GeTe, LiBeSb, and BaTiO$_3$, polar distortion localizes the bonding orbitals, reduces quantum metric, and stabilizes the soft mode of the nonpolar structure. In PbSe, pressure-induced band inversion is accompanied by an enhanced quantum metric and phonon softening without change in crystal symmetry and bonding. These results establish a common quantum geometric interpretation of bond delocalization and phonon softening across distinct bonding environments.

papers.abstract: Electron-phonon coupling is a natural source of superconductivity, but in strongly correlated materials the phonon-mediated interaction is often much weaker than the on-site Hubbard repulsion $U$. Whether, and how, it can still produce pairing when $U$ dominates is a basic open question. We address this question by studying a minimal model with an anti-Hund's coupling $J_A$: an on-site spin exchange between two orbitals or two valleys, mediated by optical phonons, that favors a local inter-orbital spin singlet. In the limit $U=+\infty$, the two-orbital Hubbard model on the triangular lattice, doped away from the insulator at $n=2$ electrons per site, reduces to a four-flavor $t$-$J_A$ model. Density-matrix renormalization group calculations find robust pairing throughout $1\le J_A/|t|\le10$, with the largest pairing gap at $J_A\sim|t|$. The Cooper pairs reside on bonds and do not come from a direct attraction provided by $J_A$, since infinite $U$ excludes on-site pairs from the Hilbert space. For $J_A\gg|t|$, the normal state is a second Fermi liquid whose small Fermi surface violates the perturbative Luttinger theorem, and a strong-coupling expansion in $t/J_A$ provides a controlled effective theory of superconductivity from this unconventional metal. Our results provide strong evidence for a strongly coupled superconductor beyond BCS theory, driven by the interplay of the kinetic energy, the phonon-mediated anti-Hund's coupling, and the strong Hubbard $U$. Finally, we discuss possible applications to magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene.

papers.summary: Recent Raman scattering experiments on bilayer nickelates have revealed pronounced spectral features in the spin-density-wave state, whose microscopic origin remains controversial, with interpretations ranging from two-magnon excitations to electronic transitions across SDW-induced gaps. papers.abstract: Recent Raman scattering experiments on bilayer nickelates have revealed pronounced spectral features in the spin-density-wave state, whose microscopic origin remains controversial, with interpretations ranging from two-magnon excitations to electronic transitions across SDW-induced gaps. Here, we demonstrate that the multiorbital electronic structure of low-pressure bilayer nickelates naturally generates distinct orbital-selective Raman signatures in different symmetry channels. Using a two-orbital bilayer model incorporating the $d_{3z^2-r^2}$ and $d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbitals in the orthorhombic structure, we analyze the electronic Raman response of the multiorbital spin-spinless double stripe SDW state and show that the $B_{2g}$ response exhibits a peak at the energy scale $(M_{z^2}+M_{x^2})/2$, associated with SDW gap openings in weakly hybridized bands. In contrast, the dominant peak in the $B_{1g}$ channel emerges at the multiorbital energy scale $(M_{z^2}^2+M_{x^2}^2)^{1/2}$, reflecting the strongly hybridized character of the relevant electronic states. These distinct energy scales provide a unified interpretation of several Raman signatures observed in La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ and offer a means of disentangling the orbital contributions to the SDW order parameters. Our results highlight that in contrast to the superconducting state, Raman peak positions in the SDW state cannot generally be identified with a single SDW gap and establish symmetry-resolved electronic Raman scattering as a sensitive probe of multiorbital density-wave order.

papers.relevance_reason: This theoretical study addresses the electronic Raman response of an ordered correlated quantum material and provides experimentally testable interpretation of its symmetry-resolved spectra.

papers.abstract: The bismuthate high-temperature superconductors have been identified as potential bipolaron systems, where hole pairs are bound to local breathing distortions of the BiO$_6$ octahedra in their metallic phase. However, obtaining definitive evidence for these quasiparticles and their excitations remains challenging. Here, we report on periodic modulations of the spectral intensities and scattering rates of quasiparticles on the Fermi surfaces of doped bismuthates Ba$_{1-x}$K$_x$BiO$_3$ and BaPb$_{1-y}$Bi$_y$O$_3$, which are reminiscent of ``hot spot'' patterns that have been observed in cuprate superconductors. We show that these features can be well described by a model where electrons couple to fluctuating density wave modulations with short-range coherence along a $(π,π,π)$-oriented wavevector. The results are consistent with the existence of a two-component fluid where unpaired electrons interact with a fluctuating density wave created by residual bipolarons and their breathing distortions of the BiO$_6$ octahedra.
papers.physics_advance: Periodic Fermi-surface spectral-intensity and scattering-rate modulations in doped bismuthates are consistent with short-range density-wave fluctuations coupled to residual bipolarons and breathing distortions.
papers.relevance_reason: The reported spectral patterns in superconducting bismuthates and their interpretation in terms of fluctuating density waves address electronic phenomena in quantum materials.

papers.summary_en: The paper proposes a minimal mechanism for spontaneous time-reversal-symmetry breaking in multiband systems proximity-coupled to a conventional s-wave superconductor, without requiring magnetic order or unconventional pairing in the components. It derives conditions and phase diagrams, including regimes with repeated transitions between time-reversal-symmetric and symmetry-broken states as a parameter varies.

papers.abstract: Recent experiments on superconducting heterostructures formed by an $s$-wave superconductor and a Dirac semimetal suggest that in these systems the superconducting state can break time-reversal symmetry even though no magnetic order or unconventional pairing is present in any of the structure's components. We present a minimal mechanism for a time-reversal-symmetry-breaking superconducting state in multiband systems proximity-coupled to a conventional $s$-wave superconductor. We derive the conditions for this state, find that it is the ground state wherever it exists, and obtain the phase diagrams. We find that in some situations the phase diagrams describe reentrant behavior: by continuously varying a parameter the system can undergo multiple transitions between a time-reversal-symmetric state and a state that spontaneously breaks time-reversal symmetry. The results help identify heterostructures that can be engineered to obtain nonreciprocal superconducting transport effects even when no magnetic field or magnetization is present.
papers.physics_advance: Shows that multiband proximity coupling to a conventional s-wave superconductor can stabilize a time-reversal-breaking superconducting ground state without magnetic order or unconventional pairing, including reentrant transitions as parameters vary.
papers.relevance_reason: It develops a theoretical mechanism and phase diagrams for spontaneous time-reversal breaking in proximity-induced superconducting heterostructures.

papers.result_en: Where the proposed state exists, it is found to be the ground state; some phase diagrams exhibit reentrant behavior with multiple transitions between symmetric and time-reversal-breaking states. The mechanism also identifies heterostructures as candidates for nonreciprocal superconducting transport without an applied magnetic field or magnetization.

papers.summary_en: This work theoretically investigates spin-superfluid transport in altermagnetic insulators on Lieb and inverse Lieb lattices. It identifies anisotropic transport and stability signatures arising from altermagnetic spin splitting and crystal-field effects.

papers.abstract: We study the spin superfluidity for Lieb and inverse Lieb lattices in altermagnets, which enables coherent transport of spin angular momentum carried by the phase of an easy-plane Néel order. The easy-plane anisotropy supplies the $U(1)$ platform, while the nonrelativistic spin splitting generates sublattice-alternating exchange imbalance with $B_{1g}$ symmetry. Via a continuum theory and Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert simulations, we find that the Goldstone mode becomes quadratic at the critical stability boundary. An axial phase gradient transfers phase-channel spectral weight to the gapped mode, whereas a diagonal flow leaves these signatures absent. The spin superfluid exhibits momentum-space anisotropy due to the chiral-splitting magnon dispersion, while strong fields or elevated temperatures suppress phase coherence. Accounting for the contribution of thermal magnons at the interface, we present that the critical spin flow varies with the injection angle under the altermagnetic crystal-field effects. The spin-superfluid decay length scales with the interfacial spin-mixing conductance, which can be measured by the spin Hall magnetoresistance and spin Seebeck effect. Our findings establish altermagnetic insulators, particularly $\mathrm{La_2O_3FeMnSe_2}$, as promising platforms for low-dissipation spin transport.
papers.physics_advance: The study predicts that altermagnetic crystal-field effects make spin-superfluid flow and its critical current direction-dependent, with a quadratic Goldstone mode at the stability boundary.
papers.relevance_reason: This theoretical and simulation study addresses coherent spin transport and collective magnetic dynamics in altermagnetic insulators, making it a substantive quantum-magnetism contribution.

papers.result_en: At the critical stability boundary, the Goldstone mode becomes quadratic; axial phase gradients transfer phase-channel spectral weight to the gapped mode, unlike diagonal flow. The critical spin flow depends on injection angle, strong fields or elevated temperatures suppress phase coherence, and the decay length scales with interfacial spin-mixing conductance.

papers.announcement_time_basis: arXiv dated batch and official 20:00 Eastern release schedule
papers.authors: Tong Liu, Hoi Chun Po
papers.summary_en: This work proposes a fractional Chern insulator in a one-band square-lattice model with plaquette-confined interactions and no single-particle quantum geometry. At one-third filling, numerical calculations show several signatures of fractional Hall order, which the authors trace to topology in the repulsive two-particle sector.

papers.abstract: A common route for realizing fractional Chern insulators (FCIs) is to engineer bands that mimic the physics of Landau levels, which serve as the single-particle topological background for the emergence of strongly correlated fractional quantum Hall states. Here we show that FCIs can also arise in a one-band model devoid of any single-particle quantum geometry. Through a systematic trivialization of the single-particle quantum geometry in FCI models that go beyond the Landau-level paradigm, we construct a single-band, interaction-only model on the square lattice, with all terms confined to individual plaquettes. At one-third filling, exact diagonalization and density-matrix renormalization-group calculations reveal a three-state low-energy manifold, a Hall conductance of $-2e^2/(3h)$, and fractional charge pumping without translation-symmetry breaking. We trace this behavior to nontrivial topology in the repulsive two-particle sector, offering a microscopic perspective on the strongly correlated origin of fractional quantum Hall order.
papers.physics_advance: It demonstrates a one-band, finite-range interaction-only model with fractional Chern insulating signatures despite lacking single-particle quantum geometry, and links the order to topology in the repulsive two-particle sector.
papers.relevance_reason: This is original theoretical work on fractional Chern insulating order and its microscopic origin in a lattice model.

papers.method_en: The authors systematically trivialize the single-particle quantum geometry of FCI models and construct an interaction-only one-band model with all terms confined to individual plaquettes. They use exact diagonalization and density-matrix renormalization-group calculations at one-third filling to probe its low-energy states and topological response.
papers.method_zh: 作者系统地平庸化分数陈绝缘体模型的单粒子量子几何，并构造一个所有项均局限于单个晶格面的纯相互作用单带模型。他们在三分之一填充下采用精确对角化和密度矩阵重整化群计算，研究其低能态和拓扑响应。
papers.result_en: The calculations reveal a three-state low-energy manifold at one-third filling. The model exhibits a Hall conductance of −2e²/(3h) and fractional charge pumping, without translation-symmetry breaking. These signatures establish fractional Hall order despite the absence of single-particle quantum geometry in the proposed model. The authors attribute the behavior to nontrivial topology in the repulsive two-particle sector, offering a microscopic account of the strongly correlated origin of the order.

papers.future_en: Further theoretical work could test the phase’s robustness beyond the reported filling and model parameters, and clarify which features of the two-particle topology are necessary for fractional order. Studies of possible experimental realizations would also assess whether the plaquette-confined interaction model can be implemented in a physical platform.

papers.tier_reason_en: The work presents a conceptually distinctive route to fractional Chern order without single-particle quantum geometry, supported by exact diagonalization and DMRG and by multiple topological diagnostics. papers.abstract: We study the ground state phase diagram of twisted bilayer graphene at magic angle as function of carrier density and the Coulomb interaction. The carrier density is varied between the fillings $ν=-2$ and $ν=-3$ and the Coulomb interaction is tuned by changing the gate distance. Our results reveal that the well established Kramers intervalley coherent (KIVC) phase near $ν=-2$, contains a hidden $f$-wave time-reversal symmetric intervalley coherent (TIVC) order, whose strength gradually increases within the metallic regime of the intervalley coherent (IVC) phase away from $ν=-2$. This finding is interesting in the light of a recent experimental work [26], where the signatures of the TIVC phase has been reported in ultra-clean samples. We further show that the system goes through multiple phase transitions as the carrier density is tuned. Near the $ν=-2$, the IVC phase is the ground state, which gives way to valley polarized phase through a second-order-like phase transition as the carrier density is lowered. Further tuning of density pushes the system into the quantum anomalous Hall phase through gradual development of the sublattice polarization. These phase transitions are accompanied by major reconstructions of the Fermi contours.

papers.abstract: Pushing ferroelectricity to the ultimate thickness limit is a central challenge for memory hardware, because conventional three-dimensional ferroelectrics degrade through depolarization and interfacial effects when thinned. Here we identify $β$-In$_2$Se$_3$, a van der Waals semiconductor regarded as centrosymmetric, as a host of bistable polar order arising from a picometre-scale distortion within each quintuple layer. The polar state has out-of-plane and in-plane components, is switched by a vertical electric field, and persists to the bilayer limit (~1.9 nm) with an estimated coercive field of 0.9 MV/cm and an apparent remanent polarization of 11.0 $μ$C/cm$^2$. Films grown by metal-organic chemical vapor deposition on 2-inch wafers yield capacitor arrays with a switching-voltage spread below 5% across 100 devices, an endurance of $10^7$ cycles and a projected ten-year retention. Because the polar state coexists with a semiconducting gap, one film serves as both the switching layer of a capacitor and the channel of a ferroelectric semiconductor transistor.
papers.physics_advance: Shows that β-In₂Se₃ has bistable, coupled in-plane and out-of-plane polar order arising from a small intralayer distortion, persisting down to the bilayer limit.
papers.relevance_reason: The work experimentally establishes a switchable polar state in a low-dimensional semiconductor, a substantive symmetry-breaking materials phenomenon beyond its device metrics.
papers.summary_zh: 本文报告了范德华半导体 β-In₂Se₃ 中的双稳态极性有序；该材料此前被认为具有中心对称性，并且极性切换可保持至双层极限。晶圆尺度薄膜及电容阵列展示了器件级的切换、耐久性和保持特性，半导体薄膜还可用作晶体管沟道。
papers.method_en: The authors investigate polar distortion and field-driven switching in β-In₂Se₃ films, including thickness-dependent behavior down to bilayers. They grow films by metal-organic chemical vapor deposition on 2-inch wafers and characterize capacitor arrays and a ferroelectric-semiconductor transistor configuration.
papers.method_zh: 作者研究 β-In₂Se₃ 薄膜中的极性畸变与电场驱动切换，包括厚度减至双层时的行为。他们通过金属有机化学气相沉积在 2 英寸晶圆上生长薄膜，并表征电容阵列及铁电半导体晶体管构型。
papers.result_en: The polar state has both out-of-plane and in-plane components, switches under a vertical electric field, and persists to approximately 1.9 nm, with an estimated coercive field of 0.9 MV/cm and apparent remanent polarization of 11.0 μC/cm². Across 100 capacitor devices, the switching-voltage spread is below 5%; the arrays reach 10⁷-cycle endurance and projected ten-year retention. The semiconducting gap allows the same film to serve as both a capacitor switching layer and a transistor channel.
papers.result_zh: 该极性态同时具有面外和面内分量，可由垂直电场切换，并在约 1.9 nm 厚度下持续存在；其估算矫顽场为 0.9 MV/cm，表观剩余极化为 11.0 μC/cm²。100 个电容器件的切换电压离散度低于 5%；阵列耐久性达到 10⁷ 次循环，预计保持时间为十年。半导体能隙使同一薄膜既可作为电容器的切换层，也可作为晶体管沟道。
papers.future_en: Further work could independently validate the polar structure and switching mechanism, and assess retention and endurance under varied operating conditions beyond the reported projections. Integrating the dual capacitor-and-channel functionality into reproducible devices would also test the proposed hardware relevance.
papers.future_zh: 后续可独立验证极性结构与切换机制，并在不同工作条件下评估超出当前预测范围的保持与耐久特性。将电容器与沟道的双重功能集成到可重复器件中，也可检验其硬件应用价值。
papers.tier_reason_en: The abstract combines an unusual ultrathin ferroelectric claim with wafer-scale growth and substantial device-array metrics, including uniformity across 100 devices and 10⁷-cycle endurance. This breadth supports a strong broad-scope tier, while the abstract alone does not establish the level of generality or validation needed to justify a higher category.
papers.tier_reason_zh: 摘要将超薄铁电性质这一重要主张与晶圆尺度生长及较充分的器件阵列指标结合起来，包括 100 个器件的均匀性和 10⁷ 次循环耐久性。这种覆盖面支持较高的综合类期刊层级；但仅凭摘要，尚不足以确认其普适性或验证程度达到更高层级所需标准。
